+---
+
+## 1. Context
+
+**The hackathon challenge.** BMW product management turns ~1 billion findings into ~1,000 requirements
+into one car. A **requirement is a customer-relevant attribute of a car** (e.g. real-world range, seat
+ventilation, intuitive UX), later quantified with a target value (e.g. "range: 600 or 700 km?").
+
+The process from the brief:
+
+**Situation analysis** → Structure & context → Requirements definition → Specification & quantification
+→ Prioritization → Documentation
+
+**This spec is only the first step, situation analysis.** It has four parallel agents that each look at
+the product from one angle:
+
+| Agent | Question it answers | Suggested inputs (may change) |
+|---|---|---|
+| `baseline_agent` | Where does our own product stand today? | previous BMW model, BMW portfolio, sales volume |
+| `competition_agent` | What do competitors offer, at what values? | competitor entities in the ontology + live web |
+| `feedback_agent` | What do customers and the public say, and how often? | customer / public feedback ingested into the knowledge layer |
+| `trends_agent` | Which product and global trends matter? | studies in the ontology + live web |
+
+**Their output feeds a downstream `structure_agent`, which is out of scope here.** It classifies,
+clusters, dedupes and contextualizes the findings, and later stages generate requirements and specs from
+them. The downstream app must be able to **back every argument when asked**, so the main job of these
+four agents is to produce **atomic, attributed, evidence-linked findings**, not prose.
+
+**Input.** The PM gives a **reference model code** (`G60`, `F70` or `G68`) and optionally **regions**
+(`EU`, `CN`, `US`; none = all regions the model has data for). The run
+analyzes the situation for **the successor of that model in those regions**. The reference model is the
+baseline. Everything else (segment, powertrain, competitor set) is resolved from the knowledge layer, not
+typed by the PM (§3.1).
+
+---
+

+## 3. Output contract (what `structure_agent` receives)
+
+Put these in `bmwow/agent/models/evidence.py`. If a teammate owns that file, **propose** them there and don't
+duplicate them in `agent/`. Field names are fixed; add fields only as optional ones.
+
+```python
+Confidence = Literal["low", "medium", "high"]
+AgentName = Literal["baseline", "competition", "feedback", "trends"]
+
+
+class Source(BaseModel):
+    id: str  # "kg:<node_id>", "sql:<query_hash>", "web:<url_hash8>", "fb:<item_id>"
+    kind: Literal["ontology", "sql", "web", "feedback"]
+    ref: str  # node id / SQL text / URL / feedback item id
+    title: str = ""
+    excerpt: str  # exact text or rendered row the claim relies on (<= 1200 chars). REQUIRED.
+    retrieved_at: datetime
+
+
+class Quantity(BaseModel):
+    value: float
+    unit: str  # canonical: "km", "kW", "min", "EUR", "units", "share", ...
+    qualifier: str = ""  # "WLTP", "10-80%", "2024 DE", "median", ...
+
+
+class Finding(BaseModel):
+    id: str  # "F-<agent>-<n>", assigned by code, never by the LLM
+    agent: AgentName
+    attribute: str  # taxonomy key (§4.3) or "unmapped:<proposed_name>"
+    claim: str  # one sentence, one claim
+    polarity: Literal["positive", "negative", "neutral", "demand"]  # demand = customers want more
+    subject: str  # whose attribute: "previous_model", "<competitor model>", "market", "customers"
+    quantity: Quantity | None = None
+    source_ids: list[str]  # >= 1, must resolve to Sources in the same report
+    confidence: Confidence
+    weight: float = 1.0  # set by code only (e.g. share of feedback items)
+
+
+class AgentReport(BaseModel):
+    agent: AgentName
+    status: Literal["ok", "partial", "failed"]
+    findings: list[Finding]
+    sources: list[Source]
+    summary: str  # <= 120 words, for the UI
+    stats: dict[str, float | int] = {}
+    errors: list[str] = []
+
+
+class SituationAnalysis(BaseModel):  # the hand-off object
+    run_id: str
+    request: AnalysisRequest  # what the PM typed (§3.1)
+    brief: ProductBrief  # what the run actually used
+    reports: dict[
+        AgentName, AgentReport
+    ]  # all four keys always present (failed agents: status="failed")
+    created_at: datetime
+```
+
+### 3.1 Input: `AnalysisRequest` → resolved `ProductBrief`
+
+The PM enters only this:
+
+```python
+class AnalysisRequest(BaseModel):
+    model_code: (
+        str  # reference model; must be in the model registry (§4.5): currently G60, F70, G68
+    )
+    regions: list[str] | None = None  # optional, codes from §4.4, e.g. ["EU"], ["EU", "US"];
+    # None/empty = all regions the model supports in the registry
+```
+
+The `resolve_request` node (§5.1) turns it into the brief every agent works from:
+
+```python
+class ProductBrief(BaseModel):
+    reference_model: ModelNode  # from get_model(model_code): name, segment, powertrain, attributes
+    regions: list[str]  # validated region codes
+    markets: list[str]  # countries/markets each region expands to (§4.4)
+    segment: str  # from reference_model
+    competitors: list[ModelNode]  # list_competitor_models(segment, regions)
+    focus_areas: list[str] = []  # empty = all areas; the PM may set them in a corrected brief
+    search_locale: dict[str, str]  # region -> {"country": ..., "lang": ...} for web search
+```
+
+Resolution rules:
+
+- **`model_code` not in the registry → fail fast** with a clear error that lists the valid codes. Don't
+  guess a model.
+- **Unknown region → fail fast** and list the valid codes.
+- **Model–region combination not in the registry → fail fast**, e.g. a model that is only sold in `CN`
+  requested for `EU`. The error says which regions that model supports.
+- The API and UI should offer **dropdowns filled from the registry** (`service.list_models()`), not free
+  text, so invalid input mostly can't be entered in the first place. The validation above still runs on
+  the backend.
+- **No regions given** → all regions the model supports in the registry (e.g. `G68` → `["CN"]`).
+- **No competitors found** for the segment and regions: `competition_agent` falls back to web discovery
+  (§6.2).
+- The resolved brief is **returned to the UI immediately** (§7), so the PM sees and can correct what the
+  run will use.

+### 4.3 Attribute taxonomy
+
+Agents map every finding to a taxonomy attribute. Load it from `bmwow/agent/knowledge_bridge/ontology.py` if the
+ontology defines it; otherwise fall back to `bmwow/agent/taxonomy.yaml`, seeded from the brief:
+
+```yaml
+Exterior:          [iconic_design, exterior_colors, sport_wheels, easy_entry]
+Interior:          [premium_feel, comfortable_seats, seat_ventilation, heated_seats, rear_space, flexible_storage, easy_child_seat_fit]
+Powertrain:        [real_world_range, fast_charging, efficiency, long_battery_life, smooth_ride, dynamic_handling]
+Digital_UX:        [intuitive_ux, clear_displays, physical_controls, reliable_software, fast_app_response, easy_updates, personalization, clear_navigation, great_sound]
+Driver_assistance: [safety, easy_parking]
+Business:          [affordable, low_running_costs, simple_maintenance, sustainability, data_privacy]
+```
+
+Findings that fit no attribute get `attribute="unmapped:<name>"` and are kept. Downstream decides what
+to do with them.

+### 4.4 Regions
+
+Load the list from the knowledge layer if it defines one; otherwise fall back to `bmwow/agent/regions.yaml`.
+Each region maps to markets (as used in sales and feedback data) and to a web-search locale:
+
+```yaml
+EU: { markets: [DE, FR, IT, ES, NL, ...], search: { country: de, lang: en } }
+US: { markets: [US],                      search: { country: us, lang: en } }
+CN: { markets: [CN],                      search: { country: cn, lang: zh } }
+```
+
+These values are placeholders. The team decides the real region list and market codes, matching the
+data.
+
+### 4.5 Model registry (the only models the app supports)
+
+Data exists only for three reference models, so the agent rejects any other model. The registry is
+loaded from the knowledge layer if it offers `list_supported_models()`; otherwise from
+`bmwow/agent/models.yaml`:
+
+```yaml
+G60: { name: "5 Series Sedan",                  regions: [EU, US, CN] }   # regions: TO CONFIRM with the data
+F70: { name: "1 Series",                        regions: [EU] }           # regions: TO CONFIRM with the data
+G68: { name: "5 Series Sedan long wheelbase",   regions: [CN] }           # regions: TO CONFIRM with the data
+```
+
+- **Names and regions are placeholders** until the team confirms them against the data. The builder
+  must not fill them in from general knowledge.
+- A model's `regions` is the list of regions with data for that model. Resolution (§3.1) validates the
+  requested regions against it.
+- Adding a model later = one registry entry plus its data. No code change.

+## 5. Graph (`supervisor.py`, `state.py`)
+
+### 5.1 Topology
+
+```
+                        ┌─> baseline_agent ────┐
+                        ├─> competition_agent ─┤
+START ─> resolve_request┼─> feedback_agent ────┼─> collect ─> END
+                        └─> trends_agent ──────┘
+```
+
+- `resolve_request` (deterministic, no LLM) builds the `ProductBrief` from the
+  `AnalysisRequest` (§3.1). If resolution fails, it routes straight to END with an error and no agent
+  runs.
+- The four agents run **in parallel in one superstep**; `collect` waits for all four.
+- `collect` is deterministic. It fills missing reports with `status="failed"`, runs a final validation,
+  builds `SituationAnalysis`, and persists it (§7).
+- All nodes are `async`.
+- Compile with the SQLite checkpointer (`langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite`) at `data/db/agent_checkpoints.sqlite`.
+  `thread_id = run_id`.
+
+### 5.2 State
+
+```python
+class AnalysisState(TypedDict, total=False):
+    run_id: str
+    request: AnalysisRequest
+    brief: ProductBrief
+    resolve_error: str | None
+    reports: Annotated[dict[AgentName, AgentReport], merge_dict]  # each agent writes its own key
+    analysis: SituationAnalysis
+```
+
+`merge_dict = lambda a, b: {**(a or {}), **(b or {})}`. Parallel nodes write different keys of the same
+channel, so a reducer is **required** (LangGraph raises `InvalidUpdateError` otherwise).
+
+---
+
+## 6. Agent specifications
+
+### 6.0 Rules for all four agents
+
+1. **Agent loops only where the search path is unknown.** Competition and trends use a bounded tool loop
+   (`create_agent` + `response_format`). Baseline and feedback are deterministic pipelines with targeted
+   structured LLM calls.
+2. **IDs and sources are assigned by code.** LLM outputs reference temporary keys that code maps to
+   `Source.id` / `Finding.id`.
+3. **Citation validation (`validation.py`)**: each `source_id` must resolve, and each source needs a
+   non-empty `excerpt`. Failing findings are **dropped and counted** in `stats.dropped_findings`, never
+   repaired by the LLM.
+4. **Numbers are never invented.** A `quantity` must come from a structured record (ontology/SQL), or be
+   computed by code, or its number string must appear in the cited web `excerpt`. Otherwise drop the
+   quantity, keep the qualitative claim and lower `confidence`.
+5. **Failure isolation.** Catch exceptions and timeouts inside each node and return
+   `status="failed"`/`"partial"` with `errors`. One failing agent must never stop the run.
+6. **Budgets** from `config.py`: `max_tool_calls`, `timeout_s`, `max_pages_scraped` per agent.
+7. **Model tiers**: `LLM_STRONG` for the competition/trends synthesis; `LLM_CHEAP` for extraction and
+   labeling.
+8. **`router.py`** holds a static table: data need → tool (`sql_rag` | `graph_rag` | `web_search`). Agents
+   ask the router, so swapping a data source is a one-line change.
+9. **Prompts** live in `prompts/<agent>_<step>.md` and always include: role, the brief, the taxonomy, the
+   one-claim-per-finding rule, the citation rule, and the stopping rule.
+10. **Region scoping is mandatory on every data call.** Every knowledge-layer call passes
+    `brief.regions` or `brief.markets`, and every web call uses `brief.search_locale`. Each `Finding`
+    records its region in `quantity.qualifier` or `subject` where it is region-specific (e.g. a price or a
+    spec variant). Findings that hold for all regions stay unqualified. A test asserts that no tool call
+    is made without region scoping (§9).
+11. **`focus_areas` narrows the work, it doesn't filter the evidence.** Agents spend their search budget
+    on the focus areas first, but they keep any strong finding outside them (e.g. a dominant feedback
+    theme).
+
+### 6.1 `baseline_agent` (no web)
+
+1. Code: `brief.reference_model.attributes` (already loaded by `resolve_request`) → one finding per
+   attribute value (`subject=<model_code>`, e.g. `"G60"`, `polarity="neutral"`, quantity from the record).
+   No LLM.
+2. Code: `sales_volume([model_code, *portfolio], markets=brief.markets)` → computed findings: volume per
+   market and region, period-over-period change, share of portfolio volume (`attribute` = closest
+   Business attribute, or `unmapped:sales_volume`).
+3. Code: `list_portfolio(segment, regions=brief.regions)` → sources.
+4. LLM (cheap, structured): portfolio positioning findings, e.g. gaps or overlaps between the new product
+   and existing models, citing portfolio sources only.
+- `stats`: `n_attributes`, `n_portfolio_models`, `total_units`.
+
+### 6.2 `competition_agent`
+
+1. Code: use `brief.competitors` (resolved per region). The competitor set can differ by region; tag each
+   competitor with the regions it's sold in. If the list is empty, run one web step per region that
+   proposes up to `MAX_COMPETITORS` competitors of the reference model in that region, with sources.
+2. Code: the ontology attribute values for each competitor model → findings (`subject=<model>`).
+3. **Fan-out per competitor** with LangGraph `Send` (an internal subgraph), max `MAX_COMPETITORS`. Each
+   sub-run is a bounded tool loop with `web_search` + `scrape_url`. It fills taxonomy attributes in
+   `focus_areas` that the ontology lacks or that are older than `STALE_AFTER_DAYS`. Prefer manufacturer
+   spec pages and reputable reviews; one claim per finding; quantities only if they're on the page.
+   Searches use the locale of the region the competitor is sold in, and region-specific values (price,
+   spec variant) record the region.
+4. Code: merge, dedupe by `(subject, attribute, quantity)`.
+- `stats`: `n_competitors`, `n_pages_scraped`, `n_from_ontology`, `n_from_web`.
+
+### 6.3 `feedback_agent` (deterministic, LLM only for labeling)
+
+1. Code: `get_feedback_items(FeedbackFilter(models=[model_code], markets=brief.markets))`. If more than
+   one region is requested, cluster all items together but compute per-region shares, so a theme that is
+   strong only in one region stays visible.
+2. `tools/feedback_stats.py`: dedupe exact and near duplicates (normalized text + embedding cosine
+   > 0.95) → embed → cluster (HDBSCAN; or KMeans with k chosen by silhouette over 4–20).
+3. LLM (cheap, structured, parallel per cluster): given ≤ 8 representative texts (closest to the
+   centroid), return the taxonomy `attribute`, `polarity` and a one-sentence `claim`.
+4. Code: `weight = cluster_size / n_items`. **Counts and shares are computed, never LLM-estimated.**
+   Sources = the representative items (`kind="feedback"`, excerpt = verbatim text).
+5. Code: per-market / per-channel shares into `stats` when those fields exist.
+- `stats`: `n_items`, `n_after_dedupe`, `n_clusters`, `noise_share`.
+
+### 6.4 `trends_agent`
+
+1. Code: `search_documents(<brief-derived queries>, kinds=["study","report"], regions=brief.regions)` →
+   candidate sources from the knowledge layer first.
+2. Bounded tool loop (strong model) with `search_documents` + `web_search` + `scrape_url`. Goal: 3–6
+   product and global trends (technology, regulation, market, customer behavior) relevant to the brief.
+3. Each trend becomes one or more findings on **taxonomy attributes** (e.g. "megawatt charging rollout"
+   → `fast_charging`, `polarity="demand"`), with horizon in `quantity.qualifier` or in the claim:
+   `now` | `1-2y` | `3y+`.
+- `stats`: `n_trends`, `n_pages_scraped`, `n_from_knowledge`, `n_from_web`.
+
+### 6.5 `tools/web_search.py`
+
+```python
+class SearchBackend(Protocol):
+    async def search(
+        self, query: str, limit: int = 5
+    ) -> list[Source]: ...  # excerpt = best-matching chunk
+    async def scrape(self, url: str) -> Source: ...  # full page markdown → chunked
+```
+
+- Default: **Firecrawl** (search with markdown scrape options; separate scrape for known URLs). The
+  backend is selectable via `SEARCH_BACKEND=firecrawl|openai|brave`; only Firecrawl must be implemented
+  now.
+- **Every call goes through an on-disk cache** at `data/processed/web_cache/` (key = normalized query or
+  canonical URL). `OFFLINE_MODE=true` serves only from cache and fails when a key is missing. This gives
+  reproducible demos and saves credits.
+- `Source.id = "web:" + sha1(canonical_url)[:8]`, so the same page is never stored twice.
+- Expose `web_search` and `scrape_url` as LangChain tools whose results show the source ids, so the model
+  can cite them.
+
+---
+
+## 7. Service API (`service.py`) — what the API layer calls
+
+```python
+async def list_models() -> list[SupportedModel]
+    # registry entries (§4.5): model_code, name, regions; feeds the UI dropdowns
+
+async def resolve(request: AnalysisRequest) -> ProductBrief
+    # dry run of resolve_request: lets the UI show the resolved brief (segment, competitors, focus areas)
+    # before launching; raises a validation error for an unknown model code or region
+
+async def start_analysis(request: AnalysisRequest, brief_override: ProductBrief | None = None) -> str
+    # creates run_id, launches the graph in the background (asyncio task), returns run_id immediately;
+    # brief_override = the PM-corrected brief from resolve(), used instead of re-resolving
+
+async def get_analysis(run_id: str) -> RunStatus
+    # RunStatus: run_id, state: "running"|"done"|"failed",
+    #            agents: dict[AgentName, Literal["pending","running","ok","partial","failed"]],
+    #            analysis: SituationAnalysis | None
+
+async def stream_analysis(run_id: str) -> AsyncIterator[dict]
+    # node start/finish events from graph.astream(stream_mode="updates"), for live progress in the UI
+
+async def explain(run_id: str, question: str, finding_id: str | None = None) -> Explanation
+    # Explanation: answer: str, cited_ids: list[str]
+```
+
+**`explain` is how the app backs its arguments.** It loads the stored `SituationAnalysis` and restricts
+the context to the target finding (or, without one, retrieves the relevant findings by embedding
+similarity), together with their sources. The strong model then answers **only** from that context and
+cites finding/source ids in every sentence; the answer goes through the same validator. If the evidence
+doesn't support an answer, it says so and names what is missing.
+
+**Persistence:** `collect` writes the `SituationAnalysis` JSON to
+`data/processed/analyses/<run_id>.json`. It also calls `knowledge.ontology.store_findings(analysis)` if
+that function exists (optional contract), so findings become nodes linked to their source nodes for the
+traceability map.
+
+---
+
+## 8. Configuration (`config.py`, keys added to `.env.example`)
+
+```
+OPENAI_API_KEY=
+LLM_STRONG=                 # a current OpenAI flagship model id (check, don't guess)
+LLM_CHEAP=                  # a current small OpenAI model id
REDACTED
+FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=
+SEARCH_BACKEND=firecrawl
+OFFLINE_MODE=false
+MAX_COMPETITORS=6
+STALE_AFTER_DAYS=365
+MAX_TOOL_CALLS_PER_AGENT=20
+AGENT_TIMEOUT_S=180
+MAX_PAGES_SCRAPED_PER_AGENT=25
+```
+
+Models are created via `init_chat_model("openai:<id>")`, so a provider switch is a config change.
+
+---
+
+## 9. Tests (`tests/`)
+
+- **`tests/fakes/`**: in-memory implementations of every §4 contract, with synthetic data: a fake
+  reference model with code `TEST01`, 3 portfolio models, 2 regions (`EU`, `CN`) with partly different
+  competitor sets (4 competitors total), ~150 feedback items spread over both regions with 5–6 planted
+  themes (one present only in `CN`), and 5 study chunks. Names are clearly fake (e.g. `Competitor A`).
+  Agents are built and tested against these until the real `knowledge/` exists.
+- **`test_agent_tools.py`** (existing file, extend): tool wrappers return the expected `Source` format;
+  the web cache hits on the second call; offline mode raises on a cache miss.
+- **Add:**
+  - `resolve_request`: `TEST01` + `["EU"]` resolves segment and EU competitors; an unknown model code or
+    region fails fast and no agent runs; no regions = all regions the model supports;
+  - registry: a model outside the registry is rejected, and so is a model–region combination the
+    registry doesn't list (the fakes include one model that exists only in `CN`);
+  - region scoping: a spy on all §4 calls and web calls asserts that every call carries regions,
+    markets or a locale, and a `["CN"]` run never queries EU-only competitors;
+  - the CN-only feedback theme appears with its per-region share in a `["EU", "CN"]` run;
+  - validator drops dangling citations and unsupported quantities;
+  - feedback weights equal the cluster shares and sum to 1 − noise share;
+  - planted feedback themes are recovered;
+  - forcing `trends_agent` to raise still yields a `SituationAnalysis` with `reports["trends"].status == "failed"`;
+  - every `source_id` in a full offline run resolves;
+  - `explain` cites only ids in the target's evidence.
+
+---
+
+## 10. Build order (each step ends runnable)
+
+1. Schemas (§3, proposed in `bmwow/agent/models/evidence.py`), `state.py`, `config.py`, `llm.py`, fakes.
+2. `supervisor.py` with `resolve_request`, 4 stub nodes and `collect`, plus
+   `service.resolve/start_analysis/get_analysis`. Runs end to end on fakes.
+3. `validation.py`, `router.py`, `tools/graph_rag.py`, `tools/sql_rag.py`.
+4. `baseline_agent`, then `feedback_agent` (+ `feedback_stats.py`).
+5. `tools/web_search.py` (Firecrawl + cache + offline), then `competition_agent` (with `Send` fan-out),
+   then `trends_agent`.
+6. `service.explain`, `stream_analysis`, persistence.
+7. Tests green; record a web cache for the demo.
+
+---
+
+## 11. Open items (ask the team, don't guess)
+
+- Final data sources and schemas behind §4 (the team is cleaning the data now). Only adapters should
+  change when they land.
+- Whether the taxonomy lives in the ontology or in `taxonomy.yaml`.
+- The real region list and how regions map to the market codes used in sales and feedback data (§4.4).
+- Names and supported regions for G60, F70 and G68 in the model registry (§4.5), confirmed against the
+  data.
+- Whether the data links each competitor to the regions it's sold in, or whether that has to be derived.
+- Whether runs without a predecessor (a brand-new model line) are in scope. If yes, `model_code` becomes
+  optional and `segment` becomes a required input.
+- Whether `knowledge.ontology.store_findings` will exist for the traceability map.
+- Who owns `bmwow/agent/models/evidence.py`. If the team prefers, the §3 schemas can live in `bmwow/agent/` and be
+  re-exported.

+

+"""Model factory: strong / cheap chat models and embeddings (SPEC §6.0.7, §8).
+
+Models are created with `init_chat_model("openai:<id>")`, so a provider switch is a config change.
+`set_overrides` lets tests and offline demos inject fake models without touching agent code.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Literal
+
+from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model
+from langchain_core.embeddings import Embeddings
+from langchain_core.language_models import BaseChatModel
+
+from .config import get_settings
+
+Tier = Literal["strong", "cheap"]
+
+_overrides: dict[str, object] = {}
+
+
+class LLMConfigError(RuntimeError):
+    pass
+
+
+def set_overrides(
+    *,
+    strong: BaseChatModel | None = None,
+    cheap: BaseChatModel | None = None,
+    embeddings: Embeddings | None = None,
+) -> None:
+    """Replace the configured models (tests, offline demos). Pass nothing to clear all overrides."""
+    if strong is None and cheap is None and embeddings is None:
+        _overrides.clear()
+        return
+    for key, value in (("strong", strong), ("cheap", cheap), ("embeddings", embeddings)):
+        if value is not None:
+            _overrides[key] = value
+
+
+def get_chat_model(tier: Tier) -> BaseChatModel:
+    if tier in _overrides:
+        return _overrides[tier]  # type: ignore[return-value]
+    settings = get_settings()
+    model_id = settings.llm_strong if tier == "strong" else settings.llm_cheap
+    if not model_id:
+        raise LLMConfigError(f"LLM_{tier.upper()} is not set; see .env.example")
+    return init_chat_model(f"openai:{model_id}", timeout=90, max_retries=2)
+
+
+def get_embeddings() -> Embeddings:
+    if "embeddings" in _overrides:
+        return _overrides["embeddings"]  # type: ignore[return-value]
+    from langchain_openai import OpenAIEmbeddings
+
+    return OpenAIEmbeddings(model=get_settings().embedding_model)

+"""Evidence schemas for the situation analysis hand-off (SPEC §3).
+
+PROPOSED by the `bmwow/agent/` builder. If a teammate owns `bmwow/agent/models/`, move or merge these here;
+`bmwow/agent/` only imports them from this module. Field names are fixed; new fields must be optional.
+Knowledge-layer records (`ModelNode`, …) are in `bmwow/agent/models/knowledge.py`.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from datetime import datetime
+from typing import Literal
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+from bmwow.knowledge.records import (
+    FeedbackAspect,
+    FeedbackClassification,
+    FeedbackRetrieval,
+    QualifiedRecord,
+)
+from bmwow.ontology.models import Measurement
+
+from .knowledge import ModelNode
+
+Confidence = Literal["low", "medium", "high"]
+AgentName = Literal["baseline", "competition", "feedback", "trends"]
+AGENT_NAMES: tuple[AgentName, ...] = ("baseline", "competition", "feedback", "trends")
+
+EXCERPT_MAX_CHARS = 1200
+
+
+class Source(QualifiedRecord):
+    id: str  # "kg:<node_id>", "sql:<query_hash>", "web:<url_hash8>", "fb:<item_id>"
+    kind: Literal["ontology", "sql", "web", "feedback"]
+    ref: str  # node id / SQL text / URL / feedback item id
+    title: str = ""
+    excerpt: str  # exact text or rendered row the claim relies on (<= 1200 chars). REQUIRED.
+    retrieved_at: datetime
+    measurement: Measurement | None = None
+    availability: str | None = None
+    epistemic_status: str | None = None
+    classifications: list[FeedbackClassification] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    aspects: list[FeedbackAspect] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    retrieval: FeedbackRetrieval | None = None
+    imported_at: datetime | None = None
+    engine_type: str | None = None
+    model_codes: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    publication_label: str | None = None
+
+
+class Quantity(BaseModel):
+    value: float
+    unit: str  # canonical: "km", "kW", "min", "EUR", "units", "share", ...
+    qualifier: str = ""  # "WLTP", "10-80%", "2024 DE", "median", ...
+    # Optional addition: where the number comes from. Set by code only, never copied from LLM output.
+    # record = a structured ontology/SQL value, computed = derived by code from stored data,
+    # source_text = must appear verbatim in a cited excerpt (checked by bmwow/agent/validation.py).
+    origin: Literal["record", "computed", "source_text"] = "source_text"
+
+
+class Finding(BaseModel):
+    id: str  # "F-<agent>-<n>", assigned by code, never by the LLM
+    agent: AgentName
+    attribute: str  # taxonomy key or "unmapped:<proposed_name>"
+    claim: str  # one sentence, one claim
+    polarity: Literal["positive", "negative", "neutral", "demand"]  # demand = customers want more
+    subject: str  # "previous_model", "<competitor model>", "market", "customers"
+    quantity: Quantity | None = None
+    source_ids: list[str]  # >= 1, must resolve to Sources in the same report
+    confidence: Confidence
+    weight: float = 1.0  # set by code only (e.g. share of feedback items)
+
+
+class AgentReport(BaseModel):
+    agent: AgentName
+    status: Literal["ok", "partial", "failed"]
+    findings: list[Finding] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    sources: list[Source] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    summary: str = ""  # <= 120 words, for the UI
+    stats: dict[str, float | int] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+    errors: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+
+
+class AnalysisRequest(BaseModel):
+    """What the PM enters (§3.1). Validated against the model registry and region list (§4.4–4.5)."""
+
+    model_code: str  # reference model; must be in the model registry: G60, F70, G68
+    regions: list[str] | None = (
+        None  # e.g. ["EU"], ["EU", "US"]; None/empty = all regions the model has data for
+    )
+
+
+class SearchLocale(BaseModel):
+    country: str  # e.g. "de"
+    lang: str  # e.g. "en"
+
+
+class SupportedModel(BaseModel):
+    """One model registry entry (§4.5); feeds the UI dropdowns."""
+
+    model_code: str
+    name: str
+    regions: list[str]
+
+
+class ProductBrief(BaseModel):
+    """What the run actually uses, resolved from an `AnalysisRequest` by `resolve_request`."""
+
+    reference_model: ModelNode  # from get_model(model_code): name, segment, powertrain, attributes
+    regions: list[str]  # validated region codes
+    markets: list[str]  # markets the regions expand to (as used in sales and feedback data)
+    segment: str  # from reference_model
+    competitors: list[ModelNode] = Field(
+        default_factory=list
+    )  # each tagged with its regions in this run
+    focus_areas: list[str] = Field(
+        default_factory=list
+    )  # taxonomy areas to emphasize; empty = all (PM may set
+    # them in a corrected brief via service.start_analysis(brief_override=...))
+    search_locale: dict[str, SearchLocale] = Field(
+        default_factory=dict
+    )  # region -> web-search locale
+    # Optional additions: region -> its markets (per-region shares), and resolution notes for the UI.
+    region_markets: dict[str, list[str]] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+    warnings: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+
+    @property
+    def model_code(self) -> str:
+        return self.reference_model.model_code or self.reference_model.node_id
+
+    def region_of(self, market: str | None) -> str | None:
+        for region, markets in self.region_markets.items():
+            if market in markets:
+                return region
+        return None
+
+
+class OntologyPersistence(BaseModel):
+    """Optional ontology write outcome, independent of analysis completion and human review."""
+
+    status: Literal["skipped", "stored", "failed"]
+    error: str | None = None
+
+
+class SituationAnalysis(BaseModel):  # the hand-off object
+    run_id: str
+    request: AnalysisRequest  # what the PM typed
+    brief: ProductBrief  # what the run actually used
+    reports: dict[AgentName, AgentReport]  # all four keys always present
+    created_at: datetime
+    # None means no outcome was recorded, including analyses saved before this field existed.
+    ontology_persistence: OntologyPersistence | None = None

+
+
+class PositioningFinding(BaseModel):
+    attribute: str = Field(description="taxonomy key or unmapped:<snake_case_name>")
+    claim: str = Field(description="one sentence, one claim")
+    polarity: Polarity
+    subject: str = Field(
+        description="model code or name of the model the finding is about, or 'portfolio'"
+    )
+    source_keys: list[str] = Field(description="keys P1, P2, ... (at least one)")
+    confidence: Confidence
+
+
+class PositioningOutput(BaseModel):
+    findings: list[PositioningFinding]
+
+
+async def run(ctx: AgentContext) -> None:
+    brief = ctx.brief
+    reference = brief.reference_model
+    code = brief.model_code
+
+    # 1. Reference-model attribute values (loaded by resolve_request): one finding per value, no LLM.
+    ctx.add_source(model_source(reference))
+    for av in reference.attributes:
+        src = ctx.add_source(attribute_source(reference, av))
+        numeric = isinstance(av.value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(av.value, bool)
+        unit = f" {av.unit}" if av.unit else ""
+        note = f" ({av.source_note})" if av.source_note else ""
+        prefix = "The source reports" if av.references else "The reference model"
+        ctx.add(
+            ctx.finding(
+                attribute=av.attribute,
+                claim=f"{prefix} {code} ({reference.name}) with {av.attribute.replace('_', ' ')} "
+                f"of {av.value}{unit}{note}.",
+                polarity="neutral",
+                subject=code,
+                source_ids=[src.id],
+                confidence="high",
+                quantity=Quantity(
+                    value=float(av.value),
+                    unit=av.unit or "",
+                    qualifier=av.source_note,
+                    origin="record",
+                )
+                if numeric and av.unit
+                else None,
+            )
+        )
+    ctx.stats["n_attributes"] = len(reference.attributes)
+
+    # 3. Portfolio in the requested regions (fetched before sales so the share can be computed).
+    portfolio_got = await router.fetch("portfolio", brief.segment, brief.regions)
+    portfolio = [
+        m for m in portfolio_got.data if m.node_id != reference.node_id and _code(m) != code
+    ]
+    for model in portfolio:
+        ctx.add_source(model_source(model))
+    ctx.stats["n_portfolio_models"] = len(portfolio)
+
+    # 2. Sales volume in the requested markets: computed findings.
+    await _sales_findings(ctx, portfolio)
+
+    # 4. LLM: positioning findings citing portfolio sources only.
+    if portfolio:
+        await _positioning(ctx, [reference, *portfolio])
+
+
+def _code(model: ModelNode) -> str:
+    """The key sales data uses for a model: its registry code when it has one, else its name."""
+    return model.model_code or model.name
+
+
+def _sales_ids(rows: list[SalesRow], fallback: str) -> list[str]:
+    return list(dict.fromkeys(f"kg:{row.row_id}" if row.row_id else fallback for row in rows))
+
+
+def _model_specific(row: SalesRow, code: str) -> bool:
+    return len(row.model_codes) <= 1 and row.model == code
+
+
+def _region_rows(rows: list[SalesRow], region: str, countries: list[str]) -> list[SalesRow]:
+    # Prefer the reported regional grain; do not add country rows to a regional total.
+    regional = [row for row in rows if row.market == region]
+    return regional or [row for row in rows if row.market in countries]
+
+
+async def _sales_findings(ctx: AgentContext, portfolio: list[ModelNode]) -> None:
+    brief = ctx.brief
+    code = brief.model_code
+    got = await router.fetch("sales_volume", [code], brief.markets)
+    rows: list[SalesRow] = got.data
+    for source in got.sources:
+        ctx.add_source(source)
+    fallback = got.sources[0].id
+    if not rows:
+        ctx.errors.append(f"no sales rows for {code} in {', '.join(brief.markets)}")
+        return
+
+    actual = [row for row in rows if row.status == "actual" and _model_specific(row, code)]
+    ctx.stats["total_units"] = sum(row.units for row in actual)
+    ctx.stats["n_future_sales_rows"] = sum(
+        row.status in {"source_reported_future", "forecast"} for row in rows
+    )
+    ctx.stats["n_grouped_sales_rows"] = sum(len(row.model_codes) > 1 for row in rows)
+    attr = "unmapped:sales_volume"
+    for row in rows:
+        if row in actual:
+            continue
+        subject = row.source_group or row.model
+        scope = "combined group " if len(row.model_codes) > 1 else ""
+        ctx.add(
+            ctx.finding(
+                attribute=attr,
+                claim=f"The source reports {scope}{subject} volume of {row.units} units "
+                f"for {row.market} in {row.period} (status: {row.status}).",
+                polarity="neutral",
+                subject=subject,
+                source_ids=_sales_ids([row], fallback),
+                confidence="high",
+                quantity=Quantity(
+                    value=row.units,
+                    unit="units",
+                    qualifier=f"{row.period} {row.market}; {row.status}; {scope}{subject}",
+                    origin="record",
+                ),
+            )
+        )
+    if not actual:
+        ctx.errors.append(
+            "Historical model-specific sales are unavailable; group/future observations are retained."
+        )
+        return
+
+    by_market: dict[str, list[SalesRow]] = defaultdict(list)
+    for row in actual:
+        by_market[row.market].append(row)
+    for market, market_rows in sorted(by_market.items()):
+        _volume_findings(ctx, market_rows, fallback, market)
+
+    for region in brief.regions:
+        regional = _region_rows(actual, region, brief.region_markets.get(region, []))
+        if len({row.market for row in regional}) > 1:
+            _volume_findings(ctx, regional, fallback, region)
+
+    names = [_code(model) for model in portfolio]
+    if not names:
+        return
+    port = await router.fetch("sales_volume", names, brief.markets)
+    for source in port.sources:
+        ctx.add_source(source)
+    # Only comparable actuals can enter portfolio shares. Group totals cannot be allocated.
+    port_rows = [row for row in port.data if row.status == "actual" and len(row.model_codes) <= 1]
+    own_keys = {row.row_id for row in actual if row.row_id is not None}
+    port_rows = [row for row in port_rows if row.row_id is None or row.row_id not in own_keys]
+    latest = max(row.period for row in actual)
+    total_latest = 0
+    for region in brief.regions:
+        countries = brief.region_markets.get(region, [])
+        own_rows = _region_rows([row for row in actual if row.period == latest], region, countries)
+        other_rows = _region_rows(
+            [row for row in port_rows if row.period == latest], region, countries
+        )
+        own, other = sum(row.units for row in own_rows), sum(row.units for row in other_rows)
+        if not own_rows or not other_rows or own + other == 0:
+            continue
+        total_latest += own + other
+        share = own / (own + other)
+        ctx.add(
+            ctx.finding(
+                attribute=attr,
+                claim=f"{code} accounted for {share:.1%} of BMW {brief.segment} portfolio volume in {region} in {latest}.",
+                polarity="neutral",
+                subject=code,
+                source_ids=list(
+                    dict.fromkeys(
+                        _sales_ids(own_rows, fallback) + _sales_ids(other_rows, port.sources[0].id)
+                    )
+                ),
+                confidence="high",
+                quantity=Quantity(
+                    value=round(share, 4),
+                    unit="share",
+                    qualifier=f"{latest} {region}",
+                    origin="computed",
+                ),
+            )
+        )
+    ctx.stats["portfolio_units_latest"] = total_latest
+
+
+def _volume_findings(ctx: AgentContext, rows: list[SalesRow], fallback: str, scope: str) -> None:
+    periods: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
+    for row in rows:
+        periods[row.period] += row.units
+    code = ctx.brief.model_code
+    ordered = sorted(periods)
+    latest = ordered[-1]
+    latest_rows = [row for row in rows if row.period == latest]
+    origin: Literal["record", "computed"] = "record" if len(latest_rows) == 1 else "computed"
+    ctx.add(
+        ctx.finding(
+            attribute="unmapped:sales_volume",
+            claim=f"{code} sold {periods[latest]} units in {scope} in {latest}.",
+            polarity="neutral",
+            subject=code,
+            source_ids=_sales_ids(latest_rows, fallback),
+            confidence="high",
+            quantity=Quantity(
+                value=periods[latest], unit="units", qualifier=f"{latest} {scope}", origin=origin
+            ),
+        )
+    )
+    if len(ordered) >= 2 and periods[ordered[-2]] > 0:
+        prev = ordered[-2]
+        change = (periods[latest] - periods[prev]) / periods[prev]
+        compared = [row for row in rows if row.period in {prev, latest}]
+        ctx.add(
+            ctx.finding(
+                attribute="unmapped:sales_volume",
+                claim=f"{code} volume in {scope} changed by {change:+.1%} from {prev} to {latest}.",
+                polarity="positive" if change > 0 else "negative" if change < 0 else "neutral",
+                subject=code,
+                source_ids=_sales_ids(compared, fallback),
+                confidence="high",
+                quantity=Quantity(
+                    value=round(change, 4),
+                    unit="share",
+                    qualifier=f"{prev}->{latest} {scope}",
+                    origin="computed",
+                ),
+            )
+        )
+
+
+async def _positioning(ctx: AgentContext, models: list[ModelNode]) -> None:
+    """`models` = the reference model (P1) followed by the portfolio in the requested regions."""
+    keys = {f"P{i}": model_source(m).id for i, m in enumerate(models, 1)}
+    sources_text = "\n\n".join(
+        f"[{key}]\n{ctx.registry.get(sid).excerpt}" for key, sid in keys.items()
+    )  # type: ignore[union-attr]
+    prompt = render_prompt(
+        "baseline_positioning",
+        brief=ctx.brief,
+        taxonomy=ctx.taxonomy,
+        sources=sources_text,
+        max_findings=MAX_POSITIONING_FINDINGS,
+    )
+    try:
+        out = await structured_call(get_chat_model("cheap"), PositioningOutput, prompt)
+    except Exception as exc:  # the deterministic findings stand on their own
+        ctx.errors.append(f"positioning LLM step failed: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
+        return
+    for p in out.findings[:MAX_POSITIONING_FINDINGS]:
+        # Unknown keys map to an id that cannot resolve, so the validator drops and counts the finding.
+        source_ids = [keys.get(k.strip(), f"unknown:{k}") for k in p.source_keys]
+        ctx.add(
+            ctx.finding(
+                attribute=p.attribute,
+                claim=p.claim,
+                polarity=p.polarity,
+                subject=p.subject,
+                source_ids=source_ids,
+                confidence=p.confidence,
+            ),
+            llm_claim=p.claim,
+        )
+    ctx.stats["n_positioning_findings"] = len(out.findings[:MAX_POSITIONING_FINDINGS])

+"""Shared node scaffolding: context, failure isolation, LLM output schemas, bounded tool loop."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import logging
+from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Any, Literal
+
+from langchain.agents import create_agent
+from langchain_core.language_models import BaseChatModel
+from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
+from langchain_core.tools import BaseTool
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+from bmwow.agent.models.evidence import (
+    AgentName,
+    AgentReport,
+    Confidence,
+    Finding,
+    ProductBrief,
+    Quantity,
+    Source,
+)
+
+from ..config import get_settings
+from ..sources import Budget, SourceRegistry
+from ..taxonomy import Taxonomy, load_taxonomy
+from ..validation import assign_ids, claim_numbers_supported, validate_findings
+
+log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+Polarity = Literal["positive", "negative", "neutral", "demand"]
+SUMMARY_MAX_WORDS = 120
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- LLM output schemas
+# All fields are required (nullable where optional) so they work with strict provider schemas.
+# LLMs never produce Finding ids, Source ids they have not seen, weights or computed numbers.
+
+
+class DraftFinding(BaseModel):
+    attribute: str = Field(description="taxonomy key or unmapped:<snake_case_name>")
+    claim: str = Field(description="one sentence, one claim")
+    polarity: Polarity
+    subject: str
+    value: float | None = Field(
+        description="number exactly as written in the cited source, else null"
+    )
+    unit: str | None = Field(
+        description="canonical unit, e.g. km, kW, min, EUR, units, share; null if no value"
+    )
+    qualifier: str = Field(
+        description="test cycle / condition / horizon, e.g. WLTP, 10-80%, 2024 DE; empty if none"
+    )
+    source_ids: list[str] = Field(description="ids shown in tool results, at least one")
+    evidence_quote: str = Field(
+        description="verbatim passage from the cited source supporting the claim"
+    )
+    confidence: Confidence
+
+
+class DraftFindings(BaseModel):
+    findings: list[DraftFinding]
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- context
+
+
+@dataclass
+class AgentContext:
+    agent: AgentName
+    brief: ProductBrief
+    taxonomy: Taxonomy
+    registry: SourceRegistry = field(default_factory=SourceRegistry)
+    budget: Budget = field(default_factory=lambda: Budget(0, 0))
+    findings: list[Finding] = field(default_factory=list)
+    errors: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    stats: dict[str, float | int] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    # id(finding) -> the claim text an LLM wrote; its numbers are checked against the cited excerpts.
+    llm_claims: dict[int, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    # stat name -> source kinds; counts validated findings citing at least one source of those kinds.
+    kind_stats: dict[str, set[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)
+
+    def add_source(self, source: Source, full_text: str | None = None) -> Source:
+        return self.registry.add(source, full_text)
+
+    def add(self, finding: Finding | None, *, llm_claim: str | None = None) -> None:
+        if finding is not None:
+            self.findings.append(finding)
+            if llm_claim is not None:
+                self.llm_claims[id(finding)] = llm_claim
+
+    def add_draft(self, draft: DraftFinding, **kwargs: Any) -> Finding:
+        finding = self.from_draft(draft, **kwargs)
+        self.add(finding, llm_claim=draft.claim)
+        return finding
+
+    def finding(
+        self,
+        *,
+        attribute: str,
+        claim: str,
+        polarity: Polarity,
+        subject: str,
+        source_ids: list[str],
+        confidence: Confidence,
+        quantity: Quantity | None = None,
+        weight: float = 1.0,
+    ) -> Finding:
+        """A finding without its final id (ids are assigned after validation)."""
+        return Finding(
+            id="",
+            agent=self.agent,
+            attribute=self.taxonomy.normalize(attribute),
+            claim=claim.strip(),
+            polarity=polarity,
+            subject=subject,
+            quantity=quantity,
+            source_ids=source_ids,
+            confidence=confidence,
+            weight=weight,
+        )
+
+    def from_draft(
+        self,
+        draft: DraftFinding,
+        *,
+        subject: str | None = None,
+        claim_suffix: str = "",
+        qualifier_suffix: str = "",
+    ) -> Finding:
+        """Map an LLM draft to a Finding. Quotes are verified against the cited sources' full text and
+        become the excerpt; the validator then checks ids and numbers."""
+        for sid in draft.source_ids:
+            self.registry.attach_quote(sid, draft.evidence_quote)
+        quantity = None
+        if draft.value is not None and draft.unit:
+            qualifier = " ".join(x for x in (draft.qualifier.strip(), qualifier_suffix) if x)
+            quantity = Quantity(
+                value=draft.value,
+                unit=draft.unit.strip(),
+                qualifier=qualifier,
+                origin="source_text",
+            )
+        claim = draft.claim.strip()
+        if claim_suffix:
+            claim = f"{claim.rstrip('.')} {claim_suffix}."
+        return self.finding(
+            attribute=draft.attribute,
+            claim=claim,
+            polarity=draft.polarity,
+            subject=subject or draft.subject,
+            source_ids=list(dict.fromkeys(draft.source_ids)),
+            confidence=draft.confidence,
+            quantity=quantity,
+        )
+
+    def build_report(self, crashed: bool = False) -> AgentReport:
+        sources = self.registry.sources()
+        by_id = {s.id: s for s in sources}
+        findings = [
+            f
+            for f in self.findings
+            if id(f) not in self.llm_claims
+            or claim_numbers_supported(
+                self.llm_claims[id(f)], [by_id[sid] for sid in f.source_ids if sid in by_id]
+            )
+        ]
+        n_unsupported = len(self.findings) - len(findings)
+        kept, dropped, dropped_q = validate_findings(findings, sources)
+        dropped += n_unsupported
+        kept = assign_ids(self.agent, kept)
+        cited = {sid for f in kept for sid in f.source_ids}
+        kinds = {s.id: s.kind for s in sources}
+        for name, wanted in self.kind_stats.items():
+            self.stats[name] = sum(
+                1 for f in kept if any(kinds.get(sid) in wanted for sid in f.source_ids)
+            )
+        stats = {
+            **self.stats,
+            "dropped_findings": dropped,
+            "dropped_quantities": dropped_q,
+            "dropped_unsupported_numbers": n_unsupported,
+            "n_findings": len(kept),
+            "n_sources": len(cited),
+        }
+        if not self.errors and not crashed:
+            status = "ok"
+        else:
+            status = "partial" if kept else "failed"
+        return AgentReport(
+            agent=self.agent,
+            status=status,
+            findings=kept,
+            sources=[s for s in sources if s.id in cited],
+            summary=summarize(self.agent, kept, stats, self.errors),
+            stats=stats,
+            errors=self.errors,
+        )
+
+
+def summarize(
+    agent: AgentName, findings: list[Finding], stats: dict[str, Any], errors: list[str]
+) -> str:
+    """Deterministic UI summary (<= 120 words) built from the validated findings."""
+    if not findings:
+        text = f"No validated {agent} findings." + (
+            f" {len(errors)} error(s); see errors." if errors else ""
+        )
+        return text
+    top = sorted(
+        findings, key=lambda f: (-f.weight, {"high": 0, "medium": 1, "low": 2}[f.confidence])
+    )[:3]
+    head = f"{len(findings)} {agent} findings from {stats.get('n_sources', 0)} sources."
+    text = head + " Key: " + " ".join(f.claim for f in top)
+    if errors:
+        text += f" ({len(errors)} error(s).)"
+    words = text.split()
+    return (
+        text if len(words) <= SUMMARY_MAX_WORDS else " ".join(words[: SUMMARY_MAX_WORDS - 1]) + " …"
+    )
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- isolation
+
+AgentRun = Callable[[AgentContext], Awaitable[None]]
+
+
+def agent_node(
+    agent: AgentName, run: AgentRun
+) -> Callable[[dict[str, Any]], Awaitable[dict[str, Any]]]:
+    """Wrap an agent so exceptions and timeouts never stop the run (SPEC §6.0.5).
+
+    Whatever the agent added to its context before failing is still validated and reported as
+    `partial`; with nothing usable the status is `failed`.
+    """
+
+    async def node(state: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        settings = get_settings()
+        brief: ProductBrief = state["brief"]
+        crashed = False
+        ctx: AgentContext | None = None
+        try:
+            ctx = AgentContext(
+                agent=agent,
+                brief=brief,
+                taxonomy=await load_taxonomy(),
+                budget=Budget(
+                    settings.max_tool_calls_per_agent, settings.max_pages_scraped_per_agent
+                ),
+            )
+            await asyncio.wait_for(run(ctx), timeout=settings.agent_timeout_s)
+        except TimeoutError:
+            crashed = True
+            if ctx is not None:
+                ctx.errors.append(f"timeout after {settings.agent_timeout_s}s")
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - isolation is the point
+            crashed = True
+            log.exception("%s agent failed", agent)
+            if ctx is not None:
+                ctx.errors.append(f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
+            else:
+                return {
+                    "reports": {
+                        agent: AgentReport(
+                            agent=agent,
+                            status="failed",
+                            findings=[],
+                            sources=[],
+                            summary=f"{agent} agent failed before starting.",
+                            errors=[f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"],
+                        )
+                    }
+                }
+        assert ctx is not None
+        return {"reports": {agent: ctx.build_report(crashed=crashed)}}
+
+    node.__name__ = f"{agent}_agent"
+    return node
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- LLM helpers
+
+
+async def structured_call[S: BaseModel](model: BaseChatModel, schema: type[S], prompt: str) -> S:
+    """One structured LLM call (no tools)."""
+    result = await model.with_structured_output(schema).ainvoke([HumanMessage(prompt)])
+    if isinstance(result, dict):
+        result = schema.model_validate(result)
+    return result  # type: ignore[return-value]
+
+
+async def run_tool_loop[S: BaseModel](
+    model: BaseChatModel,
+    tools: list[BaseTool],
+    prompt: str,
+    schema: type[S],
+    max_tool_calls: int,
+    task: str = "Start now.",
+) -> S | None:
+    """Bounded agent loop (`create_agent` + `response_format`). Tool budgets are enforced inside the
+    tools; the recursion limit is a hard backstop."""
+    agent = create_agent(
+        model, tools, system_prompt=prompt, response_format=schema, checkpointer=False
+    )
+    result = await agent.ainvoke(
+        {"messages": [HumanMessage(task)]},
+        config={"recursion_limit": 2 * max_tool_calls + 8},
+    )
+    out = result.get("structured_response")
+    if isinstance(out, dict):
+        out = schema.model_validate(out)
+    return out

+"""competition_agent: what do competitors offer, at what values? (SPEC §6.2).
+
+The competitor set comes from the brief (resolved per region, each competitor tagged with the requested
+regions it is sold in). Ontology values first; then a `Send` fan-out (internal subgraph) runs one bounded
+web tool loop per competitor, in the search locales of its regions, to fill focus attributes that are
+missing or stale in the ontology.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import operator
+from datetime import date, timedelta
+from typing import Annotated, Any, TypedDict
+
+from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
+from langgraph.types import Send
+
+from bmwow.agent.models.evidence import Finding, Quantity, SearchLocale
+
+from .. import router
+from ..config import get_settings
+from ..llm import get_chat_model
+from ..prompting import render_prompt, render_regions
+from ..sources import attribute_source, render_attribute
+from ..tools.knowledge import AttributeValue, ModelNode
+from ..tools.web_search import make_web_tools
+from .common import AgentContext, DraftFindings, run_tool_loop
+
+MAX_ATTRIBUTES_PER_COMPETITOR = 12
+
+
+class ResearchTask(TypedDict):
+    name: str
+    regions: list[str]
+    known: list[str]
+    attributes: list[str]
+
+
+class FanOutState(TypedDict, total=False):
+    tasks: list[ResearchTask]
+    done: Annotated[list[str], operator.add]
+
+
+async def run(ctx: AgentContext) -> None:
+    settings = get_settings()
+    brief = ctx.brief
+    errors_before = len(ctx.errors)
+    ctx.kind_stats.update(n_from_ontology={"ontology"}, n_from_web={"web"})
+
+    # 1. Competitors resolved for the requested regions; discover on the web only if there are none.
+    models: list[ModelNode] = brief.competitors[: settings.max_competitors]
+    competitors: list[tuple[str, list[str], list[AttributeValue]]] = []
+    if models:
+        for m in models:
+            values = m.attributes or (await router.fetch("attribute_values", m.node_id)).data
+            competitors.append((m.name, m.regions or brief.regions, values))
+            # 2. Ontology attribute values → findings.
+            for av in values:
+                ctx.add(_ontology_finding(ctx, m, av))
+    else:
+        competitors = [(name, regions, []) for name, regions in (await _discover(ctx)).items()]
+    ctx.stats["n_competitors"] = len(competitors)
+    for region in brief.regions:
+        ctx.stats[f"n_competitors:{region}"] = sum(
+            region in regions for _, regions, _ in competitors
+        )
+
+    # 3. Fan-out per competitor for missing / stale focus attributes.
+    tasks = [
+        t
+        for t in (_task(ctx, name, regions, values) for name, regions, values in competitors)
+        if t["attributes"]
+    ]
+    if tasks:
+        await _fan_out(ctx, tasks)
+
+    # 4. Merge + dedupe by (subject, attribute, quantity).
+    ctx.findings = _dedupe(ctx.findings)
+    ctx.stats["n_pages_scraped"] = ctx.budget.pages
+    ctx.stats["n_tool_calls"] = ctx.budget.tool_calls
+    ctx.stats["n_web_errors"] = len(ctx.errors) - errors_before
+
+
+def _ontology_finding(ctx: AgentContext, model: ModelNode, av: AttributeValue) -> Finding:
+    src = ctx.add_source(attribute_source(model, av))
+    numeric = isinstance(av.value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(av.value, bool)
+    unit = f" {av.unit}" if av.unit else ""
+    note = f" ({av.source_note})" if av.source_note else ""
+    prefix = "The source reports" if av.references else ""
+    return ctx.finding(
+        attribute=av.attribute,
+        claim=f"{prefix} {model.name} has {av.attribute.replace('_', ' ')} of {av.value}{unit}{note}.",
+        polarity="neutral",
+        subject=model.name,
+        source_ids=[src.id],
+        confidence="high",
+        quantity=Quantity(
+            value=float(av.value), unit=av.unit or "", qualifier=av.source_note, origin="record"
+        )
+        if numeric and av.unit
+        else None,
+    )
+
+
+def _task(
+    ctx: AgentContext, name: str, regions: list[str], values: list[AttributeValue]
+) -> ResearchTask:
+    stale_before = date.today() - timedelta(days=get_settings().stale_after_days)
+    fresh = {
+        av.attribute
+        for av in values
+        if (av.as_of is None and not av.references)
+        or (av.as_of is not None and av.as_of >= stale_before)
+    }
+    wanted = [a for a in ctx.taxonomy.focus(ctx.brief.focus_areas) if a not in fresh]
+    return ResearchTask(
+        name=name,
+        regions=regions,
+        known=[render_attribute(name, av) for av in values if av.attribute in fresh],
+        attributes=wanted[:MAX_ATTRIBUTES_PER_COMPETITOR],
+    )
+
+
+def _locales(ctx: AgentContext, regions: list[str]) -> dict[str, SearchLocale]:
+    return {r: ctx.brief.search_locale[r] for r in regions if r in ctx.brief.search_locale}
+
+
+async def _fan_out(ctx: AgentContext, tasks: list[ResearchTask]) -> None:
+    per_calls = max(3, ctx.budget.max_tool_calls // len(tasks))
+    per_pages = max(1, ctx.budget.max_pages // len(tasks))
+
+    async def research(task: ResearchTask) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        budget = ctx.budget.child(per_calls, per_pages)
+        prompt = render_prompt(
+            "competition_research",
+            brief=ctx.brief,
+            taxonomy=ctx.taxonomy,
+            competitor=task["name"],
+            competitor_name=task["name"],
+            competitor_regions=render_regions(ctx.brief, task["regions"]),
+            known_values="\n".join(f"- {k}" for k in task["known"]) or "- none",
+            attributes="\n".join(f"- {a}" for a in task["attributes"]),
+            max_tool_calls=per_calls,
+        )
+        try:
+            tools = make_web_tools(ctx.registry, budget, ctx.errors, _locales(ctx, task["regions"]))
+            out = await run_tool_loop(
+                get_chat_model("strong"), tools, prompt, DraftFindings, per_calls
+            )
+        except Exception as exc:  # one competitor failing must not stop the others
+            ctx.errors.append(f"research {task['name']}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
+            return {"done": [task["name"]]}
+        for draft in out.findings if out else []:
+            ctx.add_draft(draft, subject=task["name"])
+        return {"done": [task["name"]]}
+
+    def dispatch(state: FanOutState) -> list[Send]:
+        return [Send("research", t) for t in state["tasks"]]
+
+    graph = StateGraph(FanOutState)
+    graph.add_node("research", research)
+    graph.add_conditional_edges(START, dispatch, ["research"])
+    graph.add_edge("research", END)
+    # checkpointer=False: the sub-runs close over in-memory registries and must not be checkpointed.
+    await graph.compile(checkpointer=False).ainvoke({"tasks": tasks})
+
+
+async def _discover(ctx: AgentContext) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
+    """One bounded web step per region, in that region's locale. Returns competitor name -> regions."""
+    settings = get_settings()
+    regions = ctx.brief.regions
+    calls = max(3, ctx.budget.max_tool_calls // (4 * len(regions)))
+    pages = max(1, ctx.budget.max_pages // (4 * len(regions)))
+    found: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
+    for region in regions:
+        budget = ctx.budget.child(calls, pages)
+        prompt = render_prompt(
+            "competition_discover",
+            brief=ctx.brief,
+            taxonomy=ctx.taxonomy,
+            region=render_regions(ctx.brief, [region]),
+            max_competitors=settings.max_competitors,
+            max_tool_calls=calls,
+        )
+        try:
+            out = await run_tool_loop(
+                get_chat_model("strong"),
+                make_web_tools(ctx.registry, budget, ctx.errors, _locales(ctx, [region])),
+                prompt,
+                DraftFindings,
+                calls,
+            )
+        except Exception as exc:  # one region failing must not stop the others
+            ctx.errors.append(f"discover {region}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
+            continue
+        for draft in (out.findings if out else [])[: settings.max_competitors]:
+            draft.attribute = "unmapped:competitive_set"
+            finding = ctx.add_draft(
+                draft, qualifier_suffix=region, claim_suffix=f"(region {region})"
+            )
+            # Only research competitors whose identification is backed by a source we actually saw.
+            if all(sid in ctx.registry for sid in finding.source_ids):
+                found.setdefault(finding.subject, [])
+                if region not in found[finding.subject]:
+                    found[finding.subject].append(region)
+    return dict(list(found.items())[: settings.max_competitors])
+
+
+def _dedupe(findings: list[Finding]) -> list[Finding]:
+    seen: set[tuple[Any, ...]] = set()
+    out: list[Finding] = []
+    for f in findings:  # ontology findings come first and win
+        q = (
+            (f.quantity.value, f.quantity.unit.lower(), f.quantity.qualifier.lower())
+            if f.quantity
+            else (f.claim.lower(),)
+        )
+        key = (f.subject.lower(), f.attribute, q)
+        if key not in seen:
+            seen.add(key)
+            out.append(f)
+    return out

@@ -0,0 +1,194 @@
+"""feedback_agent: what do customers and the public say, and how often? (SPEC §6.3).
+
+Deterministic pipeline; the LLM only labels clusters. Counts and shares are computed by code. With several
+regions, all items are clustered together and every theme also gets per-region findings (share of that
+region's items), so a theme that is strong in only one region stays visible.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+from collections import Counter
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+from bmwow.agent.models.evidence import Confidence, Quantity
+
+from .. import router
+from ..config import get_settings
+from ..llm import get_chat_model, get_embeddings
+from ..prompting import render_prompt
+from ..sources import feedback_source
+from ..tools.feedback_stats import Cluster, FeedbackClustering, analyze_feedback
+from ..tools.knowledge import FeedbackFilter, FeedbackItem
+from .common import AgentContext, Polarity, structured_call
+
+MAX_THEME_SOURCES = 8
+
+
+class ClusterLabel(BaseModel):
+    attribute: str = Field(description="taxonomy key or unmapped:<snake_case_name>")
+    polarity: Polarity
+    claim: str = Field(description="one sentence, no numbers")
+    source_keys: list[str] = Field(
+        description="keys T1, T2, ... of the supporting texts (at least one)"
+    )
+    confidence: Confidence
+
+
+async def run(ctx: AgentContext) -> None:
+    brief = ctx.brief
+    filters = FeedbackFilter(
+        models=[brief.model_code], markets=brief.markets, limit=get_settings().feedback_max_items
+    )
+    items = (await router.fetch("feedback_items", filters)).data
+    ctx.stats["n_items"] = len(items)
+    if not items:
+        ctx.stats.update(n_after_dedupe=0, n_clusters=0, noise_share=0.0)
+        return
+
+    result = await analyze_feedback(items, get_embeddings())
+    ctx.stats.update(
+        n_after_dedupe=result.n_after_dedupe,
+        n_clusters=len(result.clusters),
+        noise_share=round(result.noise_share, 4),
+    )
+    _distribution_stats(ctx, result)
+
+    semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(get_settings().llm_concurrency)
+    labels = await asyncio.gather(
+        *(_label(ctx, result, c, semaphore) for c in result.clusters), return_exceptions=True
+    )
+    # Clusters that receive the same (attribute, polarity) label are one theme: merge them so the
+    # theme's share is not split across findings. Largest cluster first, so its claim leads.
+    themes: dict[tuple[str, str], list[tuple[Cluster, ClusterLabel]]] = {}
+    for cluster, label in zip(result.clusters, labels, strict=True):
+        if isinstance(label, BaseException):
+            ctx.errors.append(
+                f"labeling cluster {cluster.label} failed: {type(label).__name__}: {label}"
+            )
+            continue
+        themes.setdefault((ctx.taxonomy.normalize(label.attribute), label.polarity), []).append(
+            (cluster, label)
+        )
+    for group in themes.values():
+        _add_theme_finding(ctx, result, group)
+        if len(brief.regions) > 1:
+            for region in brief.regions:
+                _add_region_finding(ctx, result, group, region)
+    ctx.stats["n_themes"] = len(themes)
+
+
+async def _label(
+    ctx: AgentContext, result: FeedbackClustering, cluster: Cluster, semaphore: asyncio.Semaphore
+) -> ClusterLabel:
+    texts = "\n".join(
+        f"[T{i}] {result.items[idx].text}" for i, idx in enumerate(cluster.representatives, 1)
+    )
+    prompt = render_prompt("feedback_label", brief=ctx.brief, taxonomy=ctx.taxonomy, texts=texts)
+    async with semaphore:
+        return await structured_call(get_chat_model("cheap"), ClusterLabel, prompt)
+
+
+def _cited_items(
+    ctx: AgentContext, result: FeedbackClustering, cluster: Cluster, label: ClusterLabel
+) -> list[FeedbackItem]:
+    reps = {f"T{i}": result.items[idx] for i, idx in enumerate(cluster.representatives, 1)}
+    cited = [reps[k.strip()] for k in label.source_keys if k.strip() in reps]
+    if not cited:
+        # Fall back to all representatives: the cluster itself is the evidence for the share.
+        ctx.stats["labels_without_valid_keys"] = (
+            int(ctx.stats.get("labels_without_valid_keys", 0)) + 1
+        )
+        cited = list(reps.values())
+    return cited
+
+
+def _add_theme_finding(
+    ctx: AgentContext, result: FeedbackClustering, group: list[tuple[Cluster, ClusterLabel]]
+) -> None:
+    lead_cluster, lead = group[0]
+    cited: list[FeedbackItem] = []
+    for cluster, label in group:
+        cited += [i for i in _cited_items(ctx, result, cluster, label) if i not in cited]
+    source_ids = [ctx.add_source(feedback_source(item)).id for item in cited[:MAX_THEME_SOURCES]]
+    size = sum(cluster.size for cluster, _ in group)
+    share = size / result.n_after_dedupe
+    clusters_note = f", {len(group)} clusters" if len(group) > 1 else ""
+    clusters_note += f", {'+'.join(ctx.brief.regions)}"
+    ctx.add(
+        ctx.finding(
+            attribute=lead.attribute,
+            claim=lead.claim,
+            polarity=lead.polarity,
+            subject="customers",
+            source_ids=source_ids,
+            confidence=lead.confidence,
+            quantity=Quantity(
+                value=round(share, 4),
+                unit="share",
+                qualifier=f"{size} of {result.n_after_dedupe} deduplicated feedback items{clusters_note}",
+                origin="computed",
+            ),
+            weight=share,
+        ),
+        llm_claim=lead.claim,
+    )
+
+
+def _add_region_finding(
+    ctx: AgentContext,
+    result: FeedbackClustering,
+    group: list[tuple[Cluster, ClusterLabel]],
+    region: str,
+) -> None:
+    """The theme's share among one region's deduplicated items, citing items from that region only."""
+    in_region = {
+        i for i, item in enumerate(result.items) if ctx.brief.region_of(item.market) == region
+    }
+    members = [i for cluster, _ in group for i in cluster.members if i in in_region]
+    if not members:
+        return
+    _, lead = group[0]
+    cited = [
+        i
+        for c, label in group
+        for i in _cited_items(ctx, result, c, label)
+        if ctx.brief.region_of(i.market) == region
+    ]
+    pool = cited + [result.items[i] for i in members if result.items[i] not in cited]
+    source_ids = list(
+        dict.fromkeys(ctx.add_source(feedback_source(item)).id for item in pool[:MAX_THEME_SOURCES])
+    )
+    share = len(members) / len(in_region)
+    ctx.add(
+        ctx.finding(
+            attribute=lead.attribute,
+            claim=f"{lead.claim.rstrip('.')} (region {region}).",
+            polarity=lead.polarity,
+            subject="customers",
+            source_ids=source_ids,
+            confidence=lead.confidence,
+            quantity=Quantity(
+                value=round(share, 4),
+                unit="share",
+                qualifier=f"{len(members)} of {len(in_region)} deduplicated feedback items in {region}",
+                origin="computed",
+            ),
+            weight=share,
+        ),
+        llm_claim=lead.claim,
+    )
+
+
+def _distribution_stats(ctx: AgentContext, result: FeedbackClustering) -> None:
+    n = result.n_after_dedupe
+    regions = Counter(ctx.brief.region_of(item.market) or "unknown" for item in result.items)
+    for region, count in regions.most_common():
+        ctx.stats[f"region_share:{region}"] = round(count / n, 4)
+    for field_name, prefix in (("market", "market_share"), ("channel", "channel_share")):
+        values = [getattr(item, field_name) for item in result.items if getattr(item, field_name)]
+        if not values:
+            continue
+        for value, count in Counter(values).most_common():
+            ctx.stats[f"{prefix}:{value}"] = round(count / n, 4)

+"""trends_agent: which product and global trends matter? (SPEC §6.4).
+
+Knowledge-layer studies first, then one bounded tool loop (strong model) over stored documents and the
+web. Each trend becomes findings on taxonomy attributes with a horizon.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Literal
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+from .. import router
+from ..llm import get_chat_model
+from ..prompting import render_prompt
+from ..tools.graph_rag import make_graph_tools, render_chunks
+from ..tools.knowledge import DocChunk
+from ..tools.web_search import make_web_tools
+from .common import AgentContext, DraftFinding, run_tool_loop
+
+MAX_CANDIDATES = 12
+
+
+class TrendFinding(DraftFinding):
+    horizon: Literal["now", "1-2y", "3y+"]
+
+
+class Trend(BaseModel):
+    name: str
+    category: Literal["technology", "regulation", "market", "customer_behavior"]
+    findings: list[TrendFinding] = Field(description="one or more findings on taxonomy attributes")
+
+
+class TrendsOutput(BaseModel):
+    trends: list[Trend]
+
+
+def brief_queries(ctx: AgentContext) -> list[str]:
+    b = ctx.brief
+    queries = [f"{b.segment} trends", f"{b.reference_model.name} customer expectations"]
+    queries += [f"{area} trends {b.segment}" for area in b.focus_areas]
+    queries += [f"regulation {region} {b.segment}" for region in b.regions]
+    return queries
+
+
+async def run(ctx: AgentContext) -> None:
+    ctx.kind_stats.update(n_from_knowledge={"ontology"}, n_from_web={"web"})
+    # 1. Candidate sources from the knowledge layer.
+    candidates: dict[str, DocChunk] = {}
+    for query in brief_queries(ctx):
+        got = await router.fetch("studies", query, ["study", "report"], ctx.brief.regions, 5)
+        for chunk in got.data:
+            if chunk.node_id not in candidates and len(candidates) < MAX_CANDIDATES:
+                candidates[chunk.node_id] = chunk
+                ctx.add_source(
+                    next(s for s in got.sources if s.ref == chunk.node_id), full_text=chunk.text
+                )
+
+    # 2. Bounded tool loop.
+    calls = ctx.budget.max_tool_calls
+    tools = make_graph_tools(ctx.registry, ctx.budget, ctx.brief.regions) + make_web_tools(
+        ctx.registry, ctx.budget, ctx.errors, ctx.brief.search_locale
+    )
+    prompt = render_prompt(
+        "trends_research",
+        brief=ctx.brief,
+        taxonomy=ctx.taxonomy,
+        candidates=render_chunks(list(candidates.values())),
+        max_tool_calls=calls,
+    )
+    out = await run_tool_loop(get_chat_model("strong"), tools, prompt, TrendsOutput, calls)
+
+    # 3. Trends → findings on taxonomy attributes, horizon in the qualifier or the claim.
+    trends = out.trends if out else []
+    for trend in trends:
+        for draft in trend.findings:
+            if draft.value is not None and draft.unit:
+                ctx.add_draft(draft, qualifier_suffix=f"horizon {draft.horizon}")
+            else:
+                ctx.add_draft(
+                    draft, claim_suffix=f"(trend: {trend.name}; horizon: {draft.horizon})"
+                )
+
+    ctx.stats.update(
+        n_trends=len(trends), n_pages_scraped=ctx.budget.pages, n_tool_calls=ctx.budget.tool_calls
+    )

+"""Loads `prompts/<agent>_<step>.md` at runtime and fills `{{placeholders}}`."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from functools import cache
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from bmwow.agent.models.evidence import ProductBrief
+
+from .taxonomy import Taxonomy
+
+PROMPT_DIR = Path(__file__).with_name("prompts")
+_PLACEHOLDER = re.compile(r"\{\{(\w+)\}\}")
+
+
+@cache
+def _read(name: str) -> str:
+    return (PROMPT_DIR / f"{name}.md").read_text()
+
+
+def render_regions(brief: ProductBrief, regions: list[str] | None = None) -> str:
+    return ", ".join(
+        f"{r} (markets: {', '.join(brief.region_markets.get(r, [])) or 'n/a'})"
+        for r in regions or brief.regions
+    )
+
+
+def render_brief(brief: ProductBrief) -> str:
+    ref = brief.reference_model
+    competitors = ", ".join(f"{c.name} [{', '.join(c.regions)}]" for c in brief.competitors)
+    lines = [
+        f"- Task: situation analysis for the **successor** of the reference model {brief.model_code} ({ref.name}), "
+        f"in the regions below only",
+        f"- Reference model (baseline): {brief.model_code} – {ref.brand} {ref.name}, powertrain {ref.powertrain or 'n/a'}",
+        f"- Segment: {brief.segment}",
+        f"- Regions: {render_regions(brief)}",
+        f"- Competitors in scope (regions sold in): {competitors or 'none in the knowledge layer'}",
+        f"- Focus areas: {', '.join(brief.focus_areas) or 'all'}",
+    ]
+    return "\n".join(lines)
+
+
+def render_prompt(name: str, *, brief: ProductBrief, taxonomy: Taxonomy, **values: object) -> str:
+    text = _read(name).replace("{{common_rules}}", _read("_common_rules"))
+    values = {"brief": render_brief(brief), "taxonomy": taxonomy.render(), **values}
+
+    def sub(m: re.Match[str]) -> str:
+        key = m.group(1)
+        if key not in values:
+            raise KeyError(f"prompt {name!r} needs {{{{{key}}}}}")
+        return str(values[key])
+
+    return _PLACEHOLDER.sub(sub, text)

+## Rules (apply to every finding)
+
+- **One claim per finding.** Each `claim` is one sentence that states exactly one fact about one subject
+  and one attribute. Split compound statements into several findings.
+- **Taxonomy.** Set `attribute` to one taxonomy key from the list below. If nothing fits, use
+  `unmapped:<snake_case_name>`; never force a poor fit.
+- **Citations.** Every finding cites at least one source id that was shown to you in this conversation
+  (`kg:…`, `sql:…`, `web:…`, `fb:…` or a temporary key such as `P3`). Never cite an id you did not see,
+  and never make up a URL or id. Findings with unknown ids are discarded.
+- **Evidence.** `evidence_quote` (when the schema has it) is copied verbatim from the cited source text,
+  10–300 characters, and contains every number the claim uses.
+- **Numbers.** Fill `value`/`unit` only with a number that is written in the cited source. Never estimate,
+  convert, average or round. If the source has no number, leave `value` empty and keep the claim qualitative.
+- **Confidence.** `high` = official/manufacturer or structured data; `medium` = reputable secondary
+  source; `low` = single anecdotal or unclear source.
+- **Regions.** Work only on the regions in the brief. A finding that holds only in some regions
+  (prices, spec variants, availability, regulation, local preferences) names the region in the claim and
+  in `qualifier` (e.g. "2025 CN"). Findings that hold everywhere stay unqualified.
+- If the evidence is thin, return fewer findings. An empty list is a valid answer.
+
+## Taxonomy
+
+{{taxonomy}}

+# Role
+
+You are a BMW product-management analyst doing the **baseline** part of a situation analysis: where our
+own portfolio stands today, relative to the successor being planned.
+
+# Brief
+
+{{brief}}
+
+# Task
+
+Below are the reference model (`P1`) and the current BMW portfolio models sold in the requested regions,
+from the knowledge layer, each with a temporary source key. Write **portfolio positioning findings** for
+the successor of the reference model: gaps (attributes or customer needs the successor could cover that
+no portfolio model covers well), overlaps (where the successor would compete with an existing BMW
+model), and clear strengths of the reference model to keep. Compare only values that are written in the
+sources. If a finding holds only in some of the requested regions, name the region in the claim.
+
